title: InTAR: Inter-Task Auto-Reconfigurable Accelerator Design for High Data Volume Variation in DNNs
problem: Modern DNNs exhibit high data volume variation (HDV) across tasks, causing FPGA accelerators with fixed execution patterns (dataflow or sequential) to suffer from pipeline stalls or frequent off-chip memory accesses.
motivation: Deep neural networks increasingly demand efficient hardware acceleration to handle growing computational requirements and memory access patterns across diverse tasks.
method: InTAR combines the computational efficiency of sequential execution with the reduced off-chip memory overhead of dataflow execution by automatically switching between patterns based on a static schedule determined before circuit design. The reconfiguration schedule is computed once based on resource constraints and problem sizes, then encoded into the hardware design to enable model-specific optimizations without runtime overhead. The design supports HLS for rapid code generation and achieves low reconfiguration latency through pre-computed switching logic.
key_novelty: Static pre-computed reconfiguration schedules encoded at circuit design time enable model-specific resource allocation and optimizations, eliminating the need for runtime schedule computation unlike previous reconfigurable accelerators.
contributions: Accelerator design methodology that automatically switches between sequential and dataflow execution patterns based on static pre-computed schedules
Circuit design approach encoding reconfiguration logic during hardware synthesis for efficient resource utilization and high clock frequency
Support for HLS-based rapid design generation for multi-task DNN kernels
Demonstrated 3.65-39.14× speedup and 1.72-10.44× DSP efficiency gains over state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators (Allo, DFX)

metrics.speedup: 1.8× vs dataflow, 7.1× vs sequential, 3.65-39.14× vs SoTA
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1.66-7.17× better power efficiency than GPUs; 1.72-10.44× DSP efficiency vs SoTA

primary_theme: Automatic execution pattern switching for heterogeneous DNN workloads on FPGAs
